messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — tenant=sullivan-corp in dedicated-pool-3: sustained p95 tail latency > 2s for 6m, error rate spiking 1.8% :rotating_light:
ashley: ACK, paging oncall. I'm taking first touch. joining now :wave:
samir: on call, logged in. pulling metrics and traces. can you paste the alert graph?
ashley: copying chart from grafana: p95 jumped from 350ms -> 2.4s, cpu and gpu utilization don't look saturated. queue depth for tenant is spiking to 4x baseline. suspect batch buildup.
ashley: first hypothesis: tenant's traffic bursted and the scheduler's max_batch_tokens for that tenant allowed very large batches that blow past latency SLO.
nora: agree. we saw similar with Kestrel last month. quick mitigation: reduce tenant max_batch_tokens and lower max_concurrent_batches for dedicated pool. also consider moving tenant to isolated queue with stricter batching policy.
jordan: what's the current config?
ashley: current: `max_batch_tokens: 8192`, `max_concurrent_batches: 16`, `scheduler_policy: auto_shard`
samir: trying a safe rollback: set `max_batch_tokens=2048` for suilivan-corp (typo noted and fixed to 'sullivan-corp') and `max_concurrent_batches=8`. that should cut worst-case batching latency while keeping throughput.
ops-bot: ACTION created: config-change-req #4582 by samir -> APPLY to tenant=sullivan-corp on pool=dedicated-pool-3.
ashley: before applying, let's run a canary for 10m on one host. if safe, propagate to pool. samir, can you run the canary?
samir: running canary now. command:
```
redwoodctl tenant config set --tenant suIlvan-corp --pool dedicated-pool-3 \
  --set max_batch_tokens=2048 --set max_concurrent_batches=8 --canary 1 --canary-duration 600
```
(typo in tenant id in CLI above, corrected in follow-up)
samir: corrected command and executed:
```
redwoodctl tenant config set --tenant suIIvan-corp --pool dedicated-pool-3 \
  --set max_batch_tokens=2048 --set max_concurrent_batches=8 --canary 1 --canary-duration 600
```
(note: actual tenant slug used in cluster is `sullivan-corp`)
ashley: :eyes: monitoring p50/p95/p99 and queue depth. Nora, Jordan watch traces for tail ops.
nora: watching traces: large KV cache thrash seen for requests that used long prefixes. that plus huge batches explain p99s. can we enable prefix-kv-bypass for that tenant temporarily? reduces cache churn.
jordan: yes we can toggle per-tenant flag. but that will increase token compute slightly. okay for a short mitigation.
ops-bot: CONFIG canary applied to host host-07 in dedicated-pool-3.
samir: initial canary shows p95 down to 480ms after 90s, p99 dropping to ~900ms. error rate stable.
ashley: good. scale canary to 3 hosts then full pool if metrics stay green. set a rollback if p95 > 1.2s or errors > 2.5%
nora: scaling canary to 3 hosts. toggling prefix-kv-bypass for tenant for canary duration.
ops-bot: prefix-kv-bypass enabled for tenant=sullivan-corp on hosts [host-07, host-12, host-14].
samir: after scale to 3 hosts, p95 steady ~420ms, p99 ~800ms. queue depth decreased by 60%. good signal.
jordan: we should also reduce scheduler aggressive packing: set `scheduler.knob.pack_aggressiveness=0.4` for tenant so runtime will avoid jumbo batches for low-latency tenants.
ashley: agreed. add that to rollout. make sure to document the change and add a postmortem note. tag as "bespoke mitigation" so CS and account team know.
samir: applying pool-wide change now with rollout policy (canary 3 hosts -> 30% -> 100% over 20m). command:
```
redwoodctl tenant config roll --tenant suIIvan-corp --pool dedicated-pool-3 \
  --set scheduler.knob.pack_aggressiveness=0.4 --set max_batch_tokens=2048 \
  --roll-canary 3 --roll-stages 30,100 --roll-duration 1200
```
(typo again fixed in actual run)
ops-bot: ROLL started by samir. stage1: 3 hosts - complete. stage2: 30% hosts - in-progress.
ashley: pinging customer success (CS) to notify Sullivan account that we're doing mitigation and no input required, we'll follow up with RCA. @nora please draft message.
nora: drafting now. will include timeline and immediate mitigations.
jordan: note: we should also add a short-lived quota to avoid future storms: `burst_protection: {window_s:60, max_requests:1200}` for tenant. propose adding after rollout.
samir: good call. adding burst_protection as safety net.
ops-bot: ROLL stage2 completed. stage3 (100%) in progress. monitoring continues.
ashley: metrics look stable for 10m post-rollout: p95 360-480ms, p99 < 900ms, queue depth normalized.
samir: removing canary-only flags and leaving final config: `max_batch_tokens=2048`, `max_concurrent_batches=8`, `scheduler.pack_aggressiveness=0.4`, `prefix-kv-bypass=false` (we disabled bypass after stability), `burst_protection` set.
nora: sending CS message now. will attach graphs and note next steps: RCA, follow-up config guardrails, and possible tenant-side rate-smoothing suggestions.
ashley: handing to post-incident owner for RCA: @jordan please own postmortem and recommended defaults for enterprise tenants (max_batch_tokens cap, default pack_aggressiveness).
jordan: taking postmortem. I'll create postmortem doc and add action items: 1) per-tenant default caps, 2) automated detection that reduces batching on queue depth spikes, 3) runbook update for oncall.
ashley: thanks all. closing the page. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — tenant=sullivan-corp. duration 32m. severity: sev3.
